table.reason: Two length cases are unanchored: a Speaking response below minimumUsefulResponseSeconds, and a Writing response over wordMax. Both are grading-consistency holes that matter when the grader runs, not when rows are created, and the correct disposition for an over-length response in a placement instrument is probably 'no penalty' - which is a rubric-design decision, not a typo. Deferred to the scorer/grading phase, where it can be decided with the grading prompt in front of us. Explicitly NOT fixed by adding a speech-rate requirement, per D2-011.

table.reason: criterionKey 'task_fulfilment' and 'organisation' are the field names the AI grader must emit, listed in aiGradingRequirements.requiredFields. Renaming them is a coordinated change across the rubric, the grading prompt and any persisted Json snapshot. The decision recorded here is to KEEP the current identifiers rather than churn them, because learner-facing text is consistently American and these are machine field names. If they are ever renamed it must happen before the first rubric row is persisted, since DiagnosticRubric.criteria is a Json snapshot column - so this is on the Step 2E checklist.

table.action: Guard rewritten as structural JSON traversal in src/modules/diagnostic/content-guards.ts. Left anchor changed from \b to (?:^|[^A-Za-z]) so underscore-embedded identifiers match; REVISION, DEF and D<n> prefixes added; Pass/Phase/Step covered; keys traversed as well as values. 34 negative fixtures across 17 awkward variants, each injected in a string value AND in an object key.

The over-claimed flag is retired. It is replaced by three distinct flags that cannot be conflated: PERSISTENCE_MAPPING_CONTRACT_DOCUMENTED=true, PERSISTENCE_MAPPING_IMPLEMENTED=true, PERSISTENCE_MAPPING_GUARD_PASS=false. The exclusion is now executable: assertNoAuthoringFields throws on any authoring field or any key that is not a real column, and 87 tests cover it.

The guard now scans the blueprint and distinguishes active from historical use: a bare CEFR code as a value is active anywhere outside a declared history field, and a CEFR token in a level-bearing field (band/level/tier/difficulty/cefrEquivalent/placement/cutoff/threshold) is active. Fixtures prove a result band of 'B2' and an item difficulty of 'A1' both fail, while legitimate rationale in cefrClaimBasis, notCefr and previousDraftDifficultyNote passes.

Full field-by-field contract written to artifacts/entry-diagnostic-v2-persistence-contract.md, plus a pure allowlist mapper with 37 tests. All three of the collisions D3-011 named were investigated against source and resolved or recorded. NOT closed: GAP-1 blocks it.

levelSystem replaced with an UNRESOLVED_DO_NOT_IMPLEMENT record. The four bands and their cutoffs were presented as an approved V2 contract; they are not. Both disagreements are stated (band count, and Intermediate 65-79 vs code >= 75), the removed values are preserved for the decision, V1 behaviour is recorded as observed-only, and no cutoff was chosen. Upper was not introduced.

Anchor 3 now scores the ordering of the content PRESENT: 'each function the writer includes is handled in a separate, ordered sentence'. Previously a task-1 response missing a function was capped at 2 under task_achievement AND made anchor 3 unreachable - the same deficiency charged twice. Fixed despite being a NOTE because it is a live double-penalty in a rubric about to be persisted.

The validator now also compares rubrics.scoringVersion when present. contentVersion remains uncompared and that is now stated rather than implied: it is a single-document field with no counterpart in the blueprint or rubrics.

'Used with days and dates, not with clock times' -> 'Used with days and dates; it does not mark a named clock time'. 'on the half hour' is a licit clock-time use of 'on', so the old wording was broader than true - in the very item whose answerRationale was rescoped for the same reason.

The dead check is replaced. findDatabaseIds traverses the parsed structure and flags any key named 'id' or matching '*Id' whose value is a number. Fixtures prove it fires on a top-level id, a nested item id, an assessmentId and a rubricId inside a criterion, and that it does not reject order, wordMin, scores, versions, draftKey or the string scaleId. A reachability test asserts findDatabaseIds({id:1}) returns one hit - the old check could not fail at all.

persistenceContract.implementation: src/modules/diagnostic/v2-import-mapper.ts - pure functions returning plain payloads, no Prisma client, no I/O. Nothing is spread; assertNoAuthoringFields throws on any authoring field or any key that is not a real DiagnosticQuestion column.
persistenceContract.testEvidence: src/modules/diagnostic/v2-import-mapper.spec.ts, 37 tests: all 25 objective items and all 4 productive tasks map cleanly, correctIndex is derived from correctAnswer for every item, intendedLevel is null for every item, unresolved passage and rubric references throw rather than writing null, and negative fixtures prove the allowlist rejects both an authoring field and an invented column.

blockingGap.problem: DiagnosticQuestion has no column for a stable authored source identity, so an import cannot be made idempotent. A re-run has nothing to match on but (assessmentId, order) or question text, both of which change when content is revised.
blockingGap.whyThisBlocks: A non-idempotent import of 29 rows into a database with a history of expensive recovery is not a risk worth taking for convenience. The fix is one additive migration, which this phase may not perform.

nonBlockingGap.decision: Not persisted. They remain authoring and review metadata. Lossless in the safe direction: no learner sees per-distractor feedback, and nothing can attach the wrong rationale to the wrong option.

persistenceContract.confidentialityEvidence: sanitizeQuestion (diagnostic.service.ts:64) returns an explicit allowlist of 12 fields containing neither correctIndex nor explanation. explanation is returned at exactly two sites, both read and confirmed: toResult (line 365) and submitAssessment (line 846), both whole-assessment result time. submitAssessment requires the full expected answer set, so answering one question discloses nothing about the rest of an unfinished diagnostic.
persistenceContract.answerRationaleDecision: answerRationale -> explanation is PERMITTED, as a decision with evidence rather than a default, because exposure is post-submission only. Conditional on Step 2E: if toResult or sanitizeQuestion is ever changed to serve partial attempts, this decision must be revisited in the same change.
persistenceContract.shuffleProof: The authored index is the canonical identity; the permutation affects display order only. getAttemptQuestionPermutation is deterministic from attemptId and questionId, so the inverse is total and lossless - no identity is inferred from display position or from option text. Proved over all 24 permutations of 4 options against all 25 objective items: the text at a display position is the option resolved for it, the rationale shown is that authored option's own rationale, the CORRECT marker lands on the key and on exactly one option, and no non-key position grades as correct.
carriedHazards: Hazard A: isDiagnosticAnswerCorrect ends with `return answer === question.correctIndex` when no permutation is passed, so a caller that forgets it compares a display index against an authored index and silently mis-grades. Not a current bug - both live callers pass it - but it fails open. Step 2E should make the permutation required for MCQ grading or throw when absent.

Hazard B: toResult returns selectedOption (a display index) next to correctOption (an authored index). Any consumer comparing them directly is wrong; isCorrect is computed correctly and is the only safe field. Either translate correctOption into the display frame or rename both.
